title: Understanding Cross-Validation
text: Cross-validation is a technique used to assess the performance of a model by dividing the data into multiple subsets. Each subset is used as a validation set while the remaining data is used for training.

title: Bias and k-Fold Cross-Validation
text: Increasing the number of folds (k) in k-fold cross-validation generally reduces the bias of the model because it allows the model to be trained and validated on more diverse subsets of the data.

title: Computational Intensity of Cross-Validation
text: Cross-validation is typically more computationally intensive than regular validation because it involves training and validating the model multiple times, once for each fold.

title: Using the Entire Dataset
text: One of the advantages of cross-validation is that it allows the model to be trained and validated on the entire dataset, providing a more comprehensive evaluation of the model's performance.

title: Cross-Validation in Production
text: Cross-validation is not typically used in production environments because it involves using validation data during the training process, which can lead to overfitting if not managed properly.
